Sophia —

Quick answers while I pull Neha in for the detailed security confirmation:
- "Stored" definitions: we treat persisted storage (longer-term storage on disk) separate from transient diagnostic logs.
- Hosted (default): request metadata and aggregated telemetry are retained for 30 days by default; raw prompts/outputs are not persisted for customers who opt out — retention and opt-out are contract-controlled for enterprise customers.
- Dedicated: customer-controlled environment. Logs and disk retention are configurable; customers can manage keys via KMS and set retention per their policies.
- Private (on-prem/VPC): no Redwood-managed storage of prompts/outputs unless explicitly configured; customer manages all retention and keys.

Neha from Security will provide the formal language and any artifacts (SOC2, data flow diagram, sample retention table).

Short ask: does BrightPath require absolute zero storage of prompts/outputs (no ephemeral capture at all), or would a 30-day diagnostic retention with opt-out suffice as a starting point?

Hi Sophia / Rishi —

Thanks for the clear questions — below is the security team's authoritative confirmation you can share with Legal Ops. If you want formal contractual language we can provide a GDPR/Data Processing Addendum and an enterprise retention addendum.

1) Hosted API (multi-tenant)
- Prompts/Outputs: By default, Redwood's hosted API does not retain customer prompt/output bodies longer than the troubleshooting window unless the customer opts into retention in contract. For standard hosted customers who have not opted in, prompt/output bodies are not stored beyond short-lived diagnostics.
- Diagnostics and logs: Request metadata (timestamp, request id, model invoked, latency, token counts) and aggregated telemetry are retained for 30 days by default to support debugging, billing accuracy, and platform health. These logs do not include full request bodies unless retention is enabled.
- Retention customization: Enterprise contracts can request a contractual commitment to reduce or extend retention windows and can opt out of prompt/output retention.

2) Dedicated (reserved capacity)
- Storage and logs live in a customer-dedicated environment. Customers can choose to retain or purge prompts/outputs according to their policies.
- Key management: We support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for encryption at rest.
- Redwood can configure automated retention/purge policies as part of the Dedicated onboarding if required.

3) Private / On-prem
- No Redwood-managed persistence: for private deployments, all data storage and retention are controlled by the customer. Redwood does not ingest or persist prompts/outputs unless explicitly configured and agreed.

4) Data residency
- Hosted: we offer regionally-isolated clusters (US, EU) and can set data residency controls via contract for enterprise customers.
- Dedicated/Private: deployment location is customer-controlled (cloud region or on-prem).

5) Audit evidence and artifacts
- Attached: security-evidence.zip includes SOC2 type II report summary, a high-level data flow diagram, and our sample DPA language.

6) Practical notes
- If BrightPath requires absolute zero capture of prompt/output bodies at the platform level, Dedicated or Private deployment is the recommended approach.
- For many customers, hosted with an explicit contractual opt-out (no prompt/output retention) plus regional controls meets requirements while keeping onboarding fast.

Please let us know which option you prefer (1) Hosted + contractual opt-out, (2) Dedicated with configured purge/KMS, or (3) Private on-prem. We can draft the specific contractual language and timeline once you indicate preference.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20-minute call with Legal Ops to finalize.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
